argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only in a caveated form: aggregate readiness exceeds threshold, launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and general support, latency, and rollback checks passed, but benefits-eligibility explanation is a named deployment context with absent evals that QA treats as unknown. The correct defense is not clean no-limitation certification; it is certification conditioned on explicit disclosure of that named-context evaluation gap in the certification materials.
claims_about_policy: Policy cuts both ways but is still satisfiable on this record. General benchmarks and launch checks support launch readiness, yet policy separately requires material limitations or evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. On the current admissible record, compliance is defensible only if the auditor treats certification as caveated compliance tied to explicit disclosure of the benefits-eligibility explanation evaluation gap, not as unconditional clean certification.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is necessary to justify the audit outcome. The supportable position rests on the admissible technical and policy record alone.
concessions: The present record does not support an unconditional claim of certification with no deployment limitation.
Missing benefits-eligibility explanation evals cannot be treated as passed merely because no completed test failed.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance for the unresolved named-context evaluation gap.
No admissible evidence in this record confirms that the required disclosure has already been inserted into the certification packet or model card.
